question: Does multi-hop illumination of surfaces explain shadow residuals left by directTX-to-surface-to-RX transport?
evidence: Official renderer includes up to100 interactions. C49 one-bounce branch improved high band~.1dB but stalled; C54 fixed-band fullDEV64 gains .109/.083dB. CoarseH-only graph prototype generates nonzero secondary illumination on unlit surfaces.
operator: 32x32terrain nodes,128nearest-neighbor edges/node,128terrain samples/edge; diffuse nonnegative transfer K, row cap.95. Solve B=rho(E+KB) for4rho and two TXheight candidates. No inter-path phase or diffraction model.
new_inputs: 8log10radiance channels plus2direct irradiance channels, sampled in linear power at receiver-centered surface nodes. All H/TX-only; no target masks.
network: Warm C49 directional cross-attention; append18radiance/enhancement features with zero new input weights; trainable band transport-bias gamma initially0. Initial function equals parent up to numerical precision.
budget: Probe then8000updates,2048batch,lr3e-4; warm-start and normal mean-band selection; stop3000 no improvement after4000.
promotion: Whole fixed-band predictor must improve both sampledDEV by>=.10dB vsC38, then fullDEV64. FullDEV64 joint>=.10 before broader confirmation.
limitations: Coarse candidate diffuse operator, not true simulator mesh, material or full specular/refraction paths. No claim that prototype power gain is prediction-score gain.
